intro: Every day the dice roll a premise and a dozen constraints, and the game has to honor all of them. Tonight's roll was seed 3899830539. Here is each roll and what came of it. Operators are standing by.

rolls.became: Pinchworth came inland in a seafood restaurant's tank and never found his way back. Now he hosts the 3 a.m. slot on Channel 61, a TV station in the desert, about as far from the sea as a crab can get. He keeps a seashell by the phone. It's for calling home.

The product is the Fold-O-Matic, which folds paper cranes that fly. They burst out of the chute and flap all over the set, and they have to go in the shipping boxes. The manual explains the rest: cranes respond to rhythm (gamelan recommended). So Pinchworth clicks his claws on the beat and the flock comes to him.
Fold a thousand paper cranes and you get a wish. Pinchworth's wish is the sea, and the bet says he needs rather more than a thousand.

The station's midnight gamelan band never went home, so there's always a beat. Gongs slide along the CALL NOW chyron; tap as each one arrives. Perfect taps herd more, and taps in a row build a streak. The beat you're judged on is the one you hear: the game reads it off the music.

Mr. Dobbs, the station manager, on line 1: sell a sky full of cranes (one quadrillion) and the station van is Pinchworth's, the only ride to the sea. Lose, and Pinchworth is the station mascot forever. There's a little suit. The meter at the top is the bet.

The Fold-O-Matic says OUT OF ORDER. Its cranes come out loose, which is the whole reason for the herding. Call Maintenance and Wanda turns up with a toolbox and a thermos, says she'll take a look from the inside, and draws the little curtain at the back. It starts working at once.

Live Demos, the infomercial's "can your old herder do THIS?" bits: a short segment that replays the show from scratch (one crane a tap, no gadgets) under a handicap. One claw behind my back (only beats 1 and 3), Lights Out (the gongs vanish and you keep time yourself), Double Time and Off the Beat (between the beats, the way the bonang interlocks).
Pass a demo and you get a FREE GIFT, but only one of two. One side always helps your claws; the other helps the Fold-O-Matic. Tap your heart out or let the machine do it: you can't have both.
From one crane a tap to a quadrillion, at $19.99 each. But Wait, There's More! doubles every order, as many times as you can afford.
About half an hour of one very long night: 3 a.m. to nearly five.

rolls.value: an ending reached by holding back
rolls.became: When the sky is full, Dobbs says it only counts if the machine does the last of it alone, live on air. Forty seconds, no claws. Every tap makes the cranes circle back to you and the clock starts over. You win by doing nothing.

The Fold-O-Matic never worked. Wanda is an octopus, and every crane was folded by hand behind that curtain, eight arms at a time, because she liked the band. The clues were on the shelf: the machine says "ow" when kicked, the second coffee mug empties itself, the warranty card is signed W. Dobbs pays out anyway (the rule said no claws, and she hasn't got any), and Wanda drives, because crabs can't reach the pedals.

Thick black ink lines, Ben-Day dots for shading, starburst sound effects (CLICK! FWOOSH! OOOH!), Bangers lettering and a speech balloon for the log. The cactus and the phone started as icon shapes and were recut as flat comic cutouts; Pinchworth, Wanda, the cranes and the machine are drawn by hand.
Cyan, teal, steel, lavender, berry and plum on a page the colour of 3 a.m.: berry for Pinchworth, cyan for paper cranes, lavender for Wanda, steel for the Fold-O-Matic.

The midnight band: saron metallophones on the core melody, a peking elaborating in eighths, kempul and a big gong at the end of every cycle, a soft kendhang drum and a tick on every beat, in G mixolydian. It keeps a steady 96 BPM all night so you can tap to it, and it fills out when the machine gets going. During demos it drops back to the essentials; for the last forty seconds, only the gong. Every sound effect is on the same scale.
Operators are standing by. Not available in stores (or in the ocean). Shipping is free; cranes fly themselves. Every price ends in .99.
